sentence_stem: Had the board been aware of the deficit,
correct_completion: it would have delayed the merger.
full_sentence: Had the board been aware of the deficit, it would have delayed the merger.
acceptable_variants: the board would have postponed the merger.
the merger would have been put on hold.

options.text: so the merger was approved in March.
options.why_wrong: This states an actual past outcome. The inverted conditional requires a hypothetical result.

options.text: the deficit was discovered by an auditor.
options.why_wrong: This describes a different event and does not give the consequence that the inverted clause requires.

options.text: it would have delayed the merger.
it was aware of the deficit already.
options.why_wrong: This repeats the condition in the past tense instead of giving its consequence, since the inverted clause already states it.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle) with a would have main clause
explanation: The inverted form 'Had the board been aware' replaces 'If the board had been aware', so the main clause needs 'would have' followed by a past participle. Learners often use a simple conditional in the main clause, because Spanish conditionals are not formed by inverting the clause in the same way.
translation: Si la junta hubiera conocido el déficit, habría retrasado la fusión.
